title: Lessons from Vietnam Veterans
coreMove: Before trying to silence a traumatic symptom, ask what survival bond it preserves and what present safety could carry that meaning differently.

exampleSpecs.audience: Wen, a resident learning how symptoms can carry grief
exampleSpecs.stakes: Nightmare relief may be offered before anyone understands what the dreams preserve.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show medication relief colliding with loyalty to dead comrades.

exampleSpecs.audience: Shane, a facilitator translating group testimony into next steps
exampleSpecs.stakes: Rage and alcohol could be treated as isolated discipline failures instead of a shared trauma pattern.

exampleSpecs.audience: Wyatt, a clinician writing up the inkblot findings
exampleSpecs.stakes: Ambiguous images might be dismissed as personality trivia instead of trauma evidence.

exampleSpecs.audience: Simran, a psychologist deciding what counts as clinical evidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: Textbook categories could erase what veterans keep reporting in the room.

exampleSpecs.audience: Liam, a nurse practitioner reviewing a failed sleep plan
exampleSpecs.stakes: A refusal can be misread as stubbornness when it is tied to grief.

exampleSpecs.audience: Franco, a teaching attending correcting a thin lesson
exampleSpecs.stakes: Residents may learn the diagnosis while missing what veterans actually reported.
